rationale: Water damage to the policyholder's own basement (flooring, drywall, and contents) originating from the policyholder's own plumbing system is clearly property damage to the insured structure and contents.
claim_summary: Sam Patel's basement has flooded with approximately 2 inches of water due to a plumbing failure, causing extensive damage to hardwood flooring, drywall (soaked to 1 foot), and stored contents. This high-severity property damage claim (estimated well over $25,000) requires immediate adjuster assessment and water mitigation to prevent further structural damage.

case_facts.description: approximately 2 inches of water across entire basement
case_facts.damage_details: hardwood floor buckled, drywall soaked to about 1 foot high, stored boxes ruined

rationale: Wind damage to the policyholder's own roof structure (shingles on back porch overhang) is straightforward property damage to the home.
claim_summary: Wind damage to back porch roof overhang resulted in loss of approximately four shingles with no water intrusion. Estimated repair cost is $400. Policyholder has homeowners premium coverage with a $2,500 deductible and $1M limit.

case_facts.description: wind blew off approximately four shingles, no water intrusion
